reason: Safe and sensible. After a missed week, the draft repeats the plan Nessa didn't run instead of moving ahead: 24, 24 and 27 min walk-runs of 2 min running and 1 min walking. That's in line with her recent ~7 km weeks, so the volume and long session don't jump and a runner coming back from a gap isn't rushed. Her body report is clear, so no referral or illness rest is needed. It fits her Mon/Wed/Sat routine and her dog walks, and every day can be run as written: set intervals, a talking pace and a flat route. The Sunday check-in asks what got in the way, which is the right way to handle missed runs without blaming her. It's accurate about the week and doesn't make anything up. It loses a point because, in what's visible, it doesn't respond to her excitement or tie the repeat week to the 15 November goal of running the whole 5K. That makes it a little generic and leaves her without a sense of how she'll get from 2-minute running bits to a continuous run.
